sections.h2: Who collects and who assesses property tax in Calloway County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
In Calloway County the Property Valuation Administrator assesses your house and the Sheriff's Office collects the tax. The sheriff's own page says the office handles more than 27 thousand tax bills and collects over 11 million dollars a year, which makes it the main tax collector for Murray and the rest of the county.

The PVA takes homestead and disability applications and answers value questions at 270-753-3482. The sheriff's tax office is at 701 Olive Street. Delinquent bills move to the county clerk after the sheriff's collection season ends, following the process laid out by the Kentucky Department of Revenue.

Calloway County covers about 385 square miles of land on the southwest border of the state, and the 2020 Census counted 37,103 people. Because Murray State University sits in Murray, a large share of the county's housing is rented, which affects who buys and sells here.

sections.h2: When is Calloway County property tax due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Under KRS 134.015, a 2% discount applies to bills paid by the early deadline, the face amount is due through December 31, and penalties start in January. The Calloway sheriff's page states that the 2% discount applies to all payments postmarked by November 15, which is two weeks earlier than the November 30 cutoff Caldwell County uses.

The schedule printed on the top right of your bill is the one that controls, since the amount rises the later you pay. State law sets the later steps for every county:

  • Payment in full from the discount deadline to December 31: the amount on the bill.
  • January 1 to January 31: 5% penalty on unpaid tax.
  • After January 31: 10% penalty on unpaid tax, plus a sheriff's add-on fee.

Bills must be paid in full in one transaction. The sheriff accepts cash, check, money order or an online credit card payment, and the office charges $50 for a returned check, with late penalties applying again when you resend. Do not mail cash.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Calloway County tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay by drop box, by mail, in person or online. The drop box is on the west side of the sheriff's building at 701 Olive Street and is open around the clock. In-person hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and you should bring the bill.

  • Mail the payment stub and a check to Calloway County Sheriff's Office, 701 Olive St., Murray, KY 42071, and include a stamped self-addressed envelope if you want a receipt.
  • Pay online through the sheriff's tax search page, where the last page lets you print a receipt.
  • Pay several bills in one payment by mail or in person, as long as each stub is included.
  • Call the tax office at (270) 761-4TAX with questions.

Pay only the single "balance due" amount shown for your payment date. The sheriff warns against sending a separate payment for each taxing district on the bill.

sections.h2: What happens to Calloway County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The seller usually pays a prorated share of the year's tax at closing, and the buyer pays the full bill when it arrives. That is how the Calloway sheriff describes it, and it tells sellers to check the closing settlement statement if there is any doubt.

If a sale closes before the bill is issued, the title company holds back or estimates the tax. Ask the sheriff's tax office for the current amount and whether any prior-year bill is open, because past-due taxes are paid at the county clerk, not at the sheriff. A mortgage company that escrows taxes still sends the owner a copy of the bill, so a seller on a loan can see how the tax was figured even though the servicer pays it.

The City of Murray also takes property tax payments through its online payments page. Ask the city whether a city bill is open on your parcel before you set a closing date, and keep the receipts from every office that was paid.

  • Get the sheriff's current balance for the parcel.
  • Ask the county clerk whether any prior-year bill is delinquent.
  • Ask the PVA whether a homestead or disability exemption is on the account.
  • Give the title company the tax bill number printed on your stub.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Calloway County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA first, then file with the county clerk after the roll closes. The tax roll is open for public inspection for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May, and the appeal to the local board must follow a conference with the PVA, according to the state's property tax calendar.

Evidence wins these hearings. The board looks at the land, the buildings, what the home would cost to build, and sales of similar homes nearby. The state's sales comparison method adjusts nearby sales for differences such as a basement, so gather three or four recent sales near your Murray street and note where your house differs.

If you do not appear before the local board after filing, you cannot take the case further, so show up with your paperwork.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply to Calloway County owners?
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who live in the home can apply for the homestead exemption. The sheriff's page sends anyone who thinks they qualify to the PVA at 270-753-3482 instead of paying first.

The state's description is specific: only one exemption per household, tied to the owner rather than the property, so a buyer from you must file their own. Totally disabled veterans with a service-connected rating do not have to refile every year.

Farm acreage is valued by what it can produce rather than by its market price, under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution. The gap between the two values can be large near town, so a seller with acres should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

sections.h2: What does the Calloway County housing market look like?
sections.html:
Calloway County homes carry a median owner-occupied value of $183,200 in the 2020 to 2024 Census estimates, well above the $118,500 figure for Caldwell County. Only 63.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and 35.8 percent of occupied units were renter-occupied in the 2020 Census.

The county was created in 1822 from Hickman County, and a 1906 fire at the courthouse destroyed almost all of its early records, which is why old title questions sometimes need extra research. Landlords with a rental near campus, heirs with a house in Murray, and owners with a vacant farmhouse can sell as-is to a cash buyer. That route avoids waiting on a buyer's financing and the repair requests that follow an inspection. A signed offer still needs the tax payoff figures above, so collect them before you accept a closing date.

faqs.q: What is the Calloway County property tax discount deadline?
faqs.a: The sheriff's page says the 2% discount applies to payments postmarked by November 15. The bill itself shows the exact schedule, and amounts increase the later you pay.

faqs.q: Where is the Calloway County Sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 701 Olive Street in Murray, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a 24-hour drop box on the west side of the building. The tax office phone is (270) 761-4TAX.

faqs.q: Can I pay Calloway County taxes by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, but the sheriff's page says credit cards are accepted only through its website. Cash, check and money order are also accepted, and cash should never go in the mail.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax bill when a Murray house sells?
faqs.a: The seller normally pays a prorated share at closing, and the buyer pays the full bill when it is issued. Your closing settlement statement shows the split.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Calloway County house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer can take the house as-is. Any unpaid property tax is settled from the sale proceeds, so ask the sheriff and county clerk for payoff amounts first.
